extracted.intended_audience: depositors/patent applicants, patent agents, and staff of culture collections handling Budapest Treaty patent deposits
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural, technical and administrative requirements for depositing biological material (microorganisms, cell lines, plasmids, viruses, etc.) under the Budapest Treaty at national/international culture collections; includes specimen formats, viability testing, forms, fees, sample furnishing and conversion rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of Microorganisms that May Be Deposited
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists of acceptable organisms and explicit exclusions (e.g., bacteria, fungi, yeasts, bacteriophages, plasmid DNAs, plant viruses, plant/animal/human cell cultures, hybridomas) and exceptions where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections state species/types they accept and specific exclusions: e.g., VTTCC accepts bacteria and fungi preservable at −150 °C or freeze-dried and only risk groups 1 or 2; CNCM accepts animal cell cultures and many microbes but excludes plant cells, P3/P4-level agents, organisms the lab cannot viability-test, and undefined/ unidentifiable mixtures; DSMZ accepts broad range including archaea, plasmids and plant cell cultures but only risk groups 1 or 2 and material preservable by lyophilisation or liquid nitrogen; NCAIM excludes viruses, phages, rickettsiae, algae, protozoa, and many cell lines. All collections reserve the right to refuse hazardous or technically unsuitable material and require material free from contamination; mixtures of >2 organisms generally not accepted, and two-component mixtures allowed only if they cannot be separated and are easily distinguishable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and Quantity (technical submission requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Required physical form and minimum quantities/replicates that depositor must supply (e.g., number of ampoules, viable units per ml, volumes or cell counts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements vary by collection and organism: VTTCC requests three active or freeze-dried cultures of same batch; CNCM requires 12 replicates (frozen or lyophilized) containing at least 10^6 viable units/ml (exceptions possible); DSMZ lists organism-specific minima (e.g., bacteriophages 2×5 ml at ≥10^9 pfu/ml; plasmid DNA 2×20 µg; animal/human cell cultures 12 ampoules with specified cell counts); NCAIM requires 25 lyophilized replicates or 3 active cultures. Collections require material free of foreign organisms and appropriate packaging/shipping according to international regulations; some collections require submission of host strains or additional material needed for identity/purity checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time Required for Viability Testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated/average time collections need to test viability for acceptance, with explicit minimums and caveats about slow-growing organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Times differ by collection and organism: VTTCC minimum 7 days (may be longer for slow growers); CNCM average times: bacteria/phages 14 days, filamentous fungi/yeasts 25 days, animal/human cell cultures 40 days, viruses (non-bacteriophages) 60 days; DSMZ ranges from 2 days up to several weeks/months depending on type (e.g., bacteria/yeasts 2 days but up to 3 weeks; plant cell cultures 3–4 weeks or up to 6 months). Depositors should expect longer testing for slow-growing or special-requirement organisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor Checks and Renewal of Stocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligations and procedures regarding how collections prepare distribution batches, retain original material, and depositor responsibilities for authenticity checks and stock renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections typically prepare their own batches by subculturing depositor-supplied material and retain a portion of the original sample. Depositors are requested to check authenticity of at least one sample from each batch prepared by the collection. New batches are prepared when necessary to renew stocks; some collections (e.g., NCAIM) ask depositors to make a new deposit to renew diminishing stocks for lyophilized material. Some types (e.g., plasmids, viruses) may not have batches prepared by the collection and so procedures vary by collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and Administrative Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Official language(s) used by the collection for forms, communications and correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each collection specifies its official language but many accept English or provide forms in English: VTTCC official language English (also accepts Finnish/Swedish), CNCM official French but English accepted and forms available in both, DSMZ official German but English accepted, NCAIM official Hungarian but accepts English/French/German/Russian. Depositors must supply written statements and completed forms in the collection's required language(s) when specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract and Depositor Undertakings (BP/1 equivalent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal/contractual obligations imposed by signing the deposit form/contract (BP/1 or local equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signing the deposit/contract form typically binds the depositor to undertake obligations such as: supply the sample and requested information; not withdraw the deposit during the required storage period; pay all required fees; authorize the collection to supply samples for patent procedure purposes; not to hold the collection liable for deterioration if stated precautions were taken; compensate collection for damages arising from dealing with the samples. Collections differ on whether they enter a separate written contract (many do) or rely on general terms and conditions accepted by signing (DSMZ uses General Terms & Conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Import and Quarantine Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and procedures related to import permits, quarantine and regulatory clearance for bringing material into the country of the collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies vary: many collections state that kinds they accept are not subject to quarantine/import restrictions but will assist or apply for permits where necessary (CNCM provides a label and will apply for authorization if needed; DSMZ will obtain permits on request for specific species). For requests to supply samples overseas, the collection will ask the requester to provide an import permit if one is required by the destination country. Collections emphasize compliance with international transport regulations for hazardous substances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making the Original Deposit — Required Forms and Notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative steps and international model forms required when making the original deposit (model BP/1, BP/4, BP/9, BP/7 etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors must complete form BP/1 or the collection's equivalent to make an original Budapest Treaty deposit; later amendments of scientific description/taxonomic designation require BP/7. Official receipt and viability statements are issued on mandatory international forms BP/4 (receipt) and BP/9 (viability statement); attestation of receipt of later indications uses BP/8. Some collections advise faxing the deposit form before shipping and can provide unofficial early notification of deposit date/accession number after positive viability testing. Collections may send copies of receipt/viability to patent agents on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converting a Previous Deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and administrative requirements for converting deposits originally made outside the Budapest Treaty into Treaty deposits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion policies differ by collection: CCM (Czech) allows conversion only if the earlier deposit was originally made for patent purposes; VTTCC and DSMZ allow conversion whether or not the earlier deposit was for patent purposes (DSMZ adds constraints if the earlier deposit is already generally available for scientific purposes—depositor may need to authorize continued availability or must make a new Budapest deposit); CNCM allows conversion if the original deposit was for patent purposes or for confidential safekeeping/security purposes. All conversions are subject to payment of the storage fee normally levied for Budapest Treaty deposits, and administrative requirements for conversion are generally the same as for an original Treaty deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making a New Deposit (subsequent deposits) and related forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and forms required when making a new deposit of the same or replacement material (model BP/2, BP/5/BP9 for new deposit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a new deposit the depositor is asked to complete the equivalent of model form BP/2 and provide copies of relevant documents per Rule 6.2. The receipt and viability statement for a new deposit are issued on BP/5 and BP/9. The same institutional contracts/conditions apply as for the original deposit, and the depositor must follow the same technical and shipping requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of Samples — Requests, entitlement proof and applicant screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures the collection follows when responding to third-party requests for samples: model request forms, entitlement proof, qualifications of requesting parties and documentation required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections advise third parties on correct request procedures and provide model request form BP/12 (and where applicable BP/13) or the industrial property office's request form if supplied. Samples are typically furnished only to recognized microbiological laboratories (not private addresses) and are furnished from batches prepared by the collection. For potentially hazardous organisms, collections withhold samples until the requester provides evidence of entitlement, appropriate authorizations, or an import permit; CNCM requires a signed declaration that the requester has made necessary notifications and has all authorizations in their country. Collections may provide copies of request forms to the depositor when proof of entitlement is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of the Depositor when Samples Are Furnished
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligation to inform depositors when samples of their deposited microorganism are supplied to third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections issue notification to the depositor on model form BP/14 when samples of the microorganism have been furnished to third parties. Notifications are typically immediate upon receipt of a request or upon sending samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cataloguing of Budapest Treaty Deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy on whether Budapest Treaty deposits are listed in the collection's public catalogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most collections explicitly state they do not list Budapest Treaty deposits in their published catalogues (in accordance with Rule 9.2 of the Treaty). Examples: CCM, VTTCC, CNCM and DSMZ do not list Budapest Treaty deposits publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of Fees and Charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees charged by collections for accession/deposit, storage (e.g., 30 years), issuance of viability statements, furnishing samples, conversion, prolongation, communication of information, and attestations; VAT and extra charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections provide itemised fee schedules and note that fees vary by organism type and service (examples in the text include CZK/EUR amounts). Fees typically exclude VAT, transport, handling and banking charges; collections may request prepayment for foreign orders. DSMZ and others list separate fees for storage, conversion, prolongation, issuance of viability statements (with/without new test), furnishing samples (plus freight), communication/attestation, and small processing fees for handling/bank charges. Tax rules (VAT/turnover tax) and handling surcharges are specified per jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance and Support for Depositors
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of written guidance, advice channels and recommendations to contact the collection prior to deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections vary in published guidance: some (DSMZ) provide specific written notes on their website and are ready to advise by phone/email; others (VTTCC, CNCM, CCM) may not publish extensive written notes but offer assistance and advice by telephone or correspondence and encourage depositors to contact them before deposit for procedural details. Collections may provide unofficial early notifications (date/accession number) after positive viability testing if requested.
